title: The `disable_classes` INI directive was removed
summary: PHP 8.5 removes the `disable_classes` php.ini directive entirely - the mechanism previously used to block specific classes from being instantiated, "as it causes various engine assumptions to be broken". Verified directly, `disable_classes` on PHP 8.4.19 is already a main-php.ini-only setting (`ini_get_all()` access level `4`, matching `disable_functions`, `doc_root`, and `extension_dir`) that application code's own `ini_set()` cannot change at runtime, returning `false` and leaving the value unchanged even today. A project that currently blocks a dangerous class through this directive loses that protection the moment it upgrades to 8.5, silently: the directive simply stops existing, nothing errors, and the previously blocked classes become instantiable again.
new_code_policy: Never configure `disable_classes` in php.ini (or via `-d disable_classes=...`) as a security control on a PHP 8.5+ target - the directive has been removed and has no effect there; PHP silently ignores it rather than erroring, so a deployment script or base image that still sets it gives no signal that the protection it is meant to provide is not actually happening. If class-level hardening is genuinely required (blocking instantiation of a dangerous class, such as one used in a known deserialization gadget chain), it must be enforced by application code - for example, a custom autoloader or a `class_exists()`-time check - rather than by an engine-level ini directive, since PHP no longer has one for this purpose.
existing_code_policy:
Search php.ini files, `-d` flags in process/container/FPM-pool startup configuration, and any other main-php.ini-equivalent configuration source for `disable_classes = ...`; do not expect to find it configured through `.htaccess`, `.user.ini`, or `ini_set()` in application code, because it never could be. Verified directly on PHP 8.4.19: `ini_get_all()` reports `disable_classes` at access level `4`, the same level as `disable_functions`, `doc_root`, and `extension_dir`, and empirically `ini_set('disable_classes', ...)` returns `false` and leaves the value unchanged (confirmed both for an empty-string and a non-empty attempted value), exactly like the other three access-level-`4` directives tested alongside it, while a genuinely runtime-settable directive such as `precision` (access level `7`) succeeds. This is a main-php.ini-only setting today and stays that way for as long as it exists; the only real configuration surface to search is php.ini itself and equivalent startup-time configuration, not application PHP source.

Once found, treat any non-empty `disable_classes` value as documentation of an existing security control that PHP 8.5 removes out from under the project: before upgrading, identify what the directive is currently blocking and why, and re-implement that protection at the application layer (for example, in a custom class-loading gate) so the control survives the upgrade instead of silently disappearing. Application code that merely *reads* the directive - `ini_get('disable_classes')`, verified directly to return the current value as a string (empty string `''` on this host, meaning no classes are currently blocked) - will start silently receiving `false` instead once the directive is removed, the same value PHP returns for any directive name that was never defined at all (verified directly against a deliberately nonexistent directive name); code that branches on the exact return value of that read, rather than just logging it, should account for `false` becoming a possible, and indistinguishable-from-"never existed", result.
guideline: Do not rely on the `disable_classes` php.ini directive for security hardening on a PHP 8.5+ target; it has been removed "as it causes various engine assumptions to be broken" and PHP silently ignores it rather than erroring. Verified directly, this was already a main-php.ini-only setting that application code's own `ini_set()` could never change (it returns `false` and leaves the value untouched, exactly like the sibling `disable_functions` directive) - the only place it can be configured is php.ini or equivalent startup configuration, and that is also the only place the upgrade's silent loss of protection can be caught in advance. Re-implement any class-blocking hardening this directive currently provides at the application layer before upgrading.
details:
UPGRADING-8.5.0 lists this under Backward Incompatible Changes -> Core: "The disable_classes INI setting has been removed as it causes various engine assumptions to be broken." (RFC: https://wiki.php.net/rfc/deprecations_php_8_5#remove_disable_classes_ini_setting)

`disable_classes` is a hardening directive: a project can list dangerous classes there (for example ones implicated in known PHP object-injection/deserialization gadget chains) so that PHP itself refuses to instantiate them, independent of anything the application code does. P0 is warranted here specifically because of how this removal fails: not with an error, not with a warning, but by the directive simply ceasing to exist - the classes it used to block become instantiable again the moment the PHP 8.5 floor is reached, with no code change, no deployment error, and no diagnostic anywhere pointing at the cause. This is a security regression that arrives purely from upgrading the PHP version, not from any change to the application.

Verified directly on PHP 8.4.19: `ini_get_all('core', true)['disable_classes']['access']` is `4`. Calibrated against directives with a known, documented access class - `precision`, `display_errors`, `max_execution_time`, and `error_reporting` (all access `7`, and all confirmed directly to accept `ini_set()` changes at runtime) versus `disable_functions`, `doc_root`, and `extension_dir` (all access `4` like `disable_classes`, and all confirmed directly to reject `ini_set()` changes - it returns `false` and leaves the value unchanged) - access level `4` on this host corresponds exactly to "cannot be changed by `ini_set()` at runtime", the behavior documented for `PHP_INI_SYSTEM`, main-php.ini-only directives. `ini_set('disable_classes', '')` and `ini_set('disable_classes', 'SomeClass')` were both verified directly to return `false` and leave `ini_get('disable_classes')` unchanged, on this PHP 8.4.19 host, today - before any removal. This means `disable_classes` was never something application PHP code could configure at runtime in the first place; the only real configuration surface, both before and after 8.5, is php.ini itself (or equivalent startup-time configuration such as a `-d` flag or a container base image's php.ini), which is exactly where an existing_code_policy audit needs to look, not in application source.

Analyzer mapping: `PHPCompatibility.IniDirectives.RemovedIniDirectives.disable_classesRemoved`. Bisected directly against the pinned analyzer (`squizlabs/php_codesniffer:3.13.6` + `phpcompatibility/php-compatibility:10.0.0-alpha2`) on two one-line fixtures, one calling `ini_get('disable_classes')` and one calling `ini_set('disable_classes', '')`: `testVersion=8.2`, `8.3`, `8.4`, and `8.2-8.4` all produced zero findings on both fixtures; `testVersion=8.5` and `8.2-8.5` both produced exactly two findings total, one per fixture, each with the message `INI directive 'disable_classes' is removed since PHP 8.5` - agreeing exactly with the UPGRADING text cited above and confirming the sniff is keyed to the same PHP 8.5 removal, not merely plausible-looking. The two findings differ in severity in a way worth recording precisely, since it is easy to misread: the *read* call site, `ini_get('disable_classes')`, is reported as `WARNING`; the *write* call site, `ini_set('disable_classes', '')`, is reported as `ERROR` - confirmed by running each fixture individually as well as together, with the severities identical either way. A reader who only skims for `ERROR`-level findings could wrongly conclude the `ini_get()` read is the safe half of this pattern; it is not exempt from the removal, it is simply rated lower by this sniff, plausibly because attempting to *change* a directive that is about to stop existing is judged more severe than merely *reading* one.

`introduced_in` and `deprecated_in` are both null and `removed_in` is "8.5" per this rule's `kind: removed` shape - no PHP 8.2, 8.3, or 8.4 UPGRADING file documents an earlier deprecation for this directive, only the 8.5 removal itself.
notes: Runtime scope verified directly on PHP 8.4.19 (2026-09-06), no diagnostic printed by an installed set_error_handler() for any call in this note: ini_get('disable_classes') = '' (currently unset). ini_get_all('core', true)['disable_classes'] = ['global_value' => '', 'local_value' => '', 'access' => 4]. ini_set('disable_classes', '') returns false, value unchanged; ini_set('disable_classes', 'stdClass') also returns false, value unchanged. Calibration against known directives (all read via ini_get_all('core', true)['<name>']['access'], then ini_set() attempted with the directive's own current value): precision=7 (ini_set succeeds, '14'->'17'), display_errors=7 (succeeds), max_execution_time=7 (succeeds), error_reporting=7 (succeeds); disable_functions=4 (ini_set returns false, unchanged), doc_root=4 (returns false, unchanged), extension_dir=4 (returns false, unchanged) - disable_classes patterns with the access=4/ini_set-fails group, not the access=7/ini_set-succeeds group. Control: ini_get('this_directive_has_never_existed_xyz') = false and ini_set(...) on it = false - the same false that ini_get('disable_classes') will return once the directive is removed in 8.5, distinct from the '' it returns today.

Analyzer bisection executed directly (2026-09-06) with `<analyzer>/vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=PHPCompatibility --runtime-set testVersion <V> --report=json --parallel=1 --extensions=php --severity=1 --no-cache -q <dir>` against two one-line fixtures (read_only.php: `$disabled = ini_get('disable_classes');`; write_only.php: `ini_set('disable_classes', '');`), run both combined and individually: testVersion=8.2 -> 0 errors, 0 warnings; testVersion=8.3 -> 0/0; testVersion=8.4 -> 0/0; testVersion=8.2-8.4 -> 0/0; testVersion=8.5 -> 1 error, 1 warning; testVersion=8.2-8.5 -> 1 error, 1 warning (2 findings total, identical whether the two fixtures are scanned together or apart). Every finding carries sniff id PHPCompatibility.IniDirectives.RemovedIniDirectives.disable_classesRemoved and message "INI directive 'disable_classes' is removed since PHP 8.5". Severity is call-site-specific, confirmed by isolating each fixture: read_only.php (ini_get) alone -> 1 WARNING, 0 ERROR; write_only.php (ini_set) alone -> 1 ERROR, 0 WARNING. A third fixture using get_cfg_var('disable_classes') instead of ini_get()/ini_set() produced zero findings at testVersion 8.2-8.5, showing the sniff's detection is keyed to the ini_get()/ini_set() call forms specifically, not to every way the directive's name can be referenced.

Evidence: UPGRADING-8.5.0, "1. Backward Incompatible Changes" -> Core: "The disable_classes INI setting has been removed as it causes various engine assumptions to be broken." RFC: https://wiki.php.net/rfc/deprecations_php_8_5#remove_disable_classes_ini_setting
